capability_descriptions.text: Answering questions, summarising and pulling facts from documents, everyday writing.
capability_descriptions.coding-agent: Fixing and changing real software on its own, checked by each project's tests.
capability_descriptions.tool-use: Calling office tools: create a document, send an email, look up a client.
capability_descriptions.speaker-labelling: Tagging each line of a transcript with who said it.
capability_descriptions.voice-output: Reading text aloud in a natural voice (narration).
capability_descriptions.images: Generating and editing pictures from a description.
capability_descriptions.memory: Keeping an assistant's notes about a person up to date without inventing or keeping rejected facts.
capability_descriptions.fine-tuning: Training a model on the box on your own examples.

halogen.name: Halogen
halogen.why: Fastest of five engines on production's model (86 tok/s on code, 18.7 s to first word at 32K, 4 Nov); closed source.

htr-vllm.name: HTR on vLLM
htr-vllm.why: Community build with its own compression: same coding quality as production (6/10 vs 5/10), about 25% slower writing.

loom.name: AMD Loom
loom.why: AMD's engine in development: 2.7 times llama.cpp on long prompts, but not faster than Halogen.

llama.cpp.name: llama.cpp
llama.cpp.why: The open-source standard; runs almost any model, so most model tests use it. About a third of Halogen's speed on production's model.

talus.name: Talus
talus.why: Community engine for this chip: 2.5 times llama.cpp on code; runs the 27B runner-up.

gufo.name: gufo
gufo.why: Community engine: second fastest on code in the 4 Nov comparison.

strata.name: Strata
strata.why: Community engine (MIT): 2.2 times llama.cpp on code; ran Hy4-Flash.

atlas.name: Atlas
atlas.why: Community engine: about 27% faster than llama.cpp here, slower than published; one mode unusable.

ciru.name: CIRU runtime
ciru.why: Community vLLM packaging for this chip; ran Inkling-2-Mini.

pyannote.name: pyannote
pyannote.why: Better general diarisation, slower; not needed for host-or-other.

kokoro.name: Kokoro
kokoro.why: Fixed voices; the opt-in narration fallback.

diffusers.name: diffusers on ROCm PyTorch
diffusers.why: Runs Qwen-Image-2.1, only with the gateway down.

audio.cpp.name: audio.cpp
audio.cpp.why: Runs the three song models tested.

cloud-api.name: cloud API
cloud-api.why: Cloud models used as comparisons and judges only.

setups.setting: Halogen's own checkpoint, community template, effort low
setups.reason: Best local result on all three coding banks (15/15, 9/10, 5/10), passed the everyday-work tests at effort low in a third of the time, and runs fastest on Halogen.
Same model, community compression: 6/10 on the hard coding bank against production's 5/10, but slower. The known-good fallback engine.
setups.role: the everyday model on the fallback engine

setups.reason: 8/10 on the bigger-fixes bank and stronger than the July model on hard knowledge work; slower than production.
Tied production at 9/10 on the bigger-fixes bank at 30.4 minutes a task; 3/10 on the hard bank.
No mistakes on fifty memory jobs, but 6.5 times slower than production and no answer on 5 of 20 updates.
setups.role: the careful but slow memory keeper

setups.reason: 2.40% word error rate on LibriSpeech, about 28 times real time on a clean clip; voice detection stops invented words over silence.
Faster but less accurate on real speech (3.35% against 2.40% word error rate).
97.2% of lines correctly tagged host or someone else on four real calls; sidesteps guessing how many speakers there are.
Better at general diarisation (6.5% against our 20.3% error on close-talk audio) but much slower; not needed for host-or-other.

setups.model: Chatterbox, voice cloned from VCTK speaker p239
setups.reason: Won the voice tests: natural British female narration, cloned on the box.
Fast and clean, a fixed voice; kept as the opt-in fallback.

setups.setting: served on request by the gateway's image service
setups.reason: Passed the image probe and a 50-image style gallery the owner assessed; runs beside the language model.
Runs and edits text well, but only with the gateway down; edits are local changes only.
The only fast song model here and ties for clearest words; the owner liked none of the styles yet. No production pick.
Clear words but slow, and its licence is non-commercial.
About 18 times slower than real time; one render failed to play.

setups.model: House-style LoRA on the July model
setups.reason: Teaches the firm's tone reliably; does not make drafts send-ready.
2.7 times llama.cpp on long prompts, but not faster than Halogen overall.
setups.role: the everyday model on AMD Loom

setups.reason: About a third of Halogen's writing speed on the same model.
Writes 37% faster than production's model on llama.cpp but solved 0 of 10 hard coding changes.
Stable but about 24 tok/s; 3/10 on the hard bank with every task at its hour limit.
The July everyday model; replaced by Flash-Next.
The earlier coding pick; solved 2 of the bigger fixes.
